name: Ophir
overview: Ophir is a male figure mentioned in Scripture as the son of Joktan. Beyond this unique attribute, there is no additional tribal or personal information provided about him in the biblical text. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Ophir' appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:29. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is given in the text, so it is presented plainly without further significance noted.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ophir as a son of Joktan, establishing a direct paternal relationship. No other family ties or relationships are recorded beyond this connection in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Ophir's significance lies chiefly in his place within the genealogical record of Genesis, linking him to Joktan. This connection situates him within the broader narrative of the descendants of Noah, emphasizing the continuity of God's providential plan through successive generations. Although the text does not elaborate on his personal deeds or role, his mention contributes to the biblical understanding of human lineage and God's unfolding purpose.
